book.why: LMT is the only name two members picked separately: Ophelia for the defense bid after a blowout quarter ($7.94 vs $7.20 EPS, a record $230B backlog), Cecil for a clean beat that is already reported at 21.5x trailing, so it gets the maximum weight.

JNJ leads Ophelia's defensive healthcare call, sitting at 100% of its 52-week high after a +4.1% week, and as low-beta cash-flow pharma it wins on relative value with the 10-year at 4.7%, with no report until October.
PGR is Cecil's strongest value case at 11.3x trailing with EPS still growing 10%, the 4.70% 10-year raises the income it earns on the premiums it holds, and it does not report until October.

COP is the cleanest way to own Ophelia's top call, energy as the book's hedge against the oil-and-yields shock, outside the XOM/CVX blackout and with no report until Aug 6, but it is held to 15% because a ceasefire, the risk she names herself, could wipe out the war premium with RSI at 86.

CAT is Marky's most textbook setup, exactly 1.5 channel widths below a channel rising 113% a year (the depth where his score is full), at 89% of its high after a +1.15% week with only 3.6% weekly volatility, sized at 15% because the weekly MACD turn has not come yet.

rationale: LMT is the strongest signal on the page because two members reached it separately and for different reasons, so it takes the 30% cap, and the other four slots go to the cleanest pick by each member's own test: JNJ and COP for Ophelia's healthcare and energy calls, PGR for Cecil's value screen and CAT for Marky's channel pullback. Where the members disagree, I side with Ophelia over Cecil on gold, because NEM is down 14% in 12 weeks and at 72% of its high despite the war, and Cecil himself holds it only as a trade; on Financials I took Cecil's PGR, whose rate case holds up against the hawkish-FOMC curve risk Ophelia raised, and kept JPM, a bank more exposed to that risk, as an alternate alongside LNG, which has the same energy call as COP but long-term contracts that soften a ceasefire. Among Marky's names CAT sits exactly at the 1.5-width depth where his score is full and has low volatility, while RKLB and GOOGL sit deeper, nearer his 2.5-width break, and are still falling, INOD swings 28% a week, and TSM scored lower on his own screen. No name reports this week, the book is fully invested because no member argued for cash, and I have no memory of how this week turned out and used none.
